, if we want to use VAE models to extract features from high-dimensional data lying on or close to a low-dimensional manifold, then we must accept that the gradients of the energy function may be unbounded.
, for a certain class of autoencoder models, unbounded gradients are not only a symptom of overfitting, they are also a necessary condition for avoiding overfitting.
The main takeaway from our work is that

, when applied to data on or near a manifold, the VAE energy is fundamentally ill-posed without unbounded gradients, and that such gradients are a natural consequence of a model that seeks to simultaneously avoid overfitting and underfitting.

, while it is certainly true that large parameter gradients can lead to numerical instabilities during training, the VAE energy landscape itself can be understood as a regularization mechanism that is necessary to avoid both over- and underegularization in certain cases.
infinite gradients in VAE models are not a bug, but a feature, and should not be avoided.
